subject: Re: Pilot credits & pricing — follow-up and burn-rate check
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finapps.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot credits & pricing — follow-up

Hi Sam — great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

- Goal: run a 2-week pilot of Redwood inference on your customer support reranking flow to validate latency and unit economics.
- Expected traffic for pilot: ~150k–300k tokens/day (peak ~50k) — roughly 1M–2.1M tokens over 14 days.
- Post-pilot target: scale to 8–12M tokens/month if metrics look good.
- Your budget signal: team mentioned target ~ $400–$600 / 1M tokens for production economics (including batching/caching benefits).

Ask from our side: can you confirm the conservative & optimistic token-volume scenarios (daily/monthly) and any hard budget constraints? That helps me size pilot credits and suggest config (batching, cache TTLs, model variant).

I've attached a short pilot plan and an initial pricing summary for typical throughput profiles. Proposed next steps:
1) I'll provision an initial credit grant for the pilot once you confirm volumes.
2) We'll kick off a short onboarding call (30 min) to set up keys, routes, and dashboard access — Marcus will join for runtime tuning.
3) Check-in after 3 business days to review pilot burn-rate and tweak batching/seq length.

Would you like the pilot credits to be enough for the conservative estimate (~1M tokens) or the optimistic (~2M)?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: pilot_plan_v1.pdf, pricing_summary.xlsx
From: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finapps.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finapps.io>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot credits & pricing — follow-up

Thanks Marissa — nice to meet you too. Quick answers below: 

- Pilot: we expect closer to the optimistic side given our daily test load — plan for ~180k–220k tokens/day. So 2M tokens total for 10–12 days is realistic.
- Post-pilot target: if latency and quality meet expectations, we expect to ramp to ~10M tokens/month in month 1, then 12M+ by month 3.
- Budget: our procurement guideline is target $500 / 1M tokens for production. We can stretch for pilot to evaluate value, but procurement will look for unit cost closer to that target for long-term commits.

Please provision credits for 2M tokens for the pilot. Procurement is cc'd — they will need the pricing summary and a short statement of the credit terms (expiry, refundable/non-refundable).

Sam
Sam Johnson | Head of ML Platform, FinApps
sam.johnson@finapps.io | (415) 555-0127
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finapps.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finapps.io>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot credits & pricing — follow-up

Thanks for the quick confirmation, Sam — that's helpful.

Credit grant: I can approve a 2,000,000-token pilot credit for FinApps (one-time, valid for 30 days). Terms: non-refundable, applies to usage on the pilot route/profile we configure. We'll track consumption in the Console and provide a burn-rate summary daily.

Notes on unit economics we recommend for the pilot to approximate production:
- Use a smaller model variant for initial throughput tests (same family but quantized) to measure latency/cost.
- Enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (if applicable) — this typically reduces tokens billed and effective $/1M by ~15–30% depending on hit rate.
- Batching policy: start with conservative batch size (8–16) and adjust once we see latency tail.

Attachments: I've attached a short Pilot Scope doc (poc_scope.docx) and updated pricing_summary.xlsx with example effective $/1M ranges at different cache hit rates.

Next steps:
- Marcus will set up the service account and route with your infra team tomorrow morning.
- We'll schedule the 30-min onboarding call for Fri 2/20 or Mon 2/23 — what's best for you?
- I'll send a short credit grant statement and the pilot SLA notes for Procurement to review.

If Procurement needs a standard MSA addendum or a PO, loop me in and I can fast-track approvals with our legal ops.

Best,
Marissa
From: Procurement <procurement@finapps.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finapps.io>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot credits & pricing — follow-up

Hi Marissa — we have a couple of quick procurement items before we accept the pilot credits: 
1) Credit expiry confirmation (we prefer 45 days).
2) Short statement confirming credits are non-transferable and apply only to pilot route.
3) Invoice or PO flow if we convert to paid commitment — example SOW language and billing contact.

If you can send a one-page credit statement and the updated pricing sheet, we can sign off on our side.

Procurement (FinApps)
procurement@finapps.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement <procurement@finapps.io>, Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finapps.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot credits & pricing — follow-up

Hi — thanks for the checklist. Quick answers and next steps below: 

1) Credit expiry: we can extend to 45 days for FinApps.
2) Credit statement: attached one-page credit_grant_statement.pdf (summary below).
   - Amount: 2,000,000 tokens
   - Validity: 45 days from issuance (expires 2026-04-10)
   - Scope: Non-transferable; applies only to FinApps pilot project and configured pilot route(s).
   - Refunds: Credits are non-refundable; unused credits simply expire.
3) If you convert to paid commitment, invoicing follows standard Redwood billing (we'll provide PO and invoice to your AP contact). Example SOW language and billing contact attached in pricing_summary.xlsx.

Operational notes:
- We'll monitor daily burn and share a short summary after 48 hours and 7 days. If you hit >80% of credits before day 7, we'll schedule a rapid tuning session (batching/kv-cache/seq-len) to optimize effective $/1M.
- Targeted unit economics: with caching and quantization we typically see effective ranges of $350–$550 / 1M tokens for workloads like yours; exact numbers depend on cache hit rate and avg sequence length.

Onboarding: Marcus will reach out to set up keys and the onboarding call today.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments (sent): credit_grant_statement.pdf, pricing_summary.xlsx, pilot_plan_v1.pdf
